dashboard_line: Audited 77 skills: zero startup token cost (lazy load). Data skills (vision/audio/db-reconstruct) use free models + API options. Faerie2 culturally tight to Claude CLI. Open models need context injection + onboarding template. Recommend bridge adapter pattern.

executive_summary.key_finding: Faerie2 system optimized for Claude CLI (Agent() tool) but architecturally decoupled from Claude-specific code. Free model integration present but incomplete for open-source model onboarding.

section_1_token_cost_analysis.title: TOKEN COST ANALYSIS: Do Skills Cost Tokens at Rest?
section_1_token_cost_analysis.answer: NO — Skills cost zero tokens at rest. Only invoked skills consume tokens.

details.rationale: Claude Code CLI loads skill metadata (SKILL.md, ≤2KB) only when invoked or during CLI startup discovery. Skills are not pre-cached in context.
evidence: All 77 skills under /mnt/d/0LOCAL/.claude/skills/ are standalone directories with .md + Python execution
Skills use subprocess/subprocess.run() pattern for isolation — no shared memory pool
Global settings.json declares hook-based execution (Post-tool, SubagentStop, Stop) — not memory-resident
Manifest-first architecture means skill output stored in forensics/, not context
No SKILL_REGISTRY.json or master loader pre-ingesting all skill metadata

load_strategy_by_type.on_demand_skills: Default. Loaded when invoked (/spawn, /data-ingest, /vision-ingest). No startup tax.
load_strategy_by_type.hook_driven_skills: audit-coc, audit-session, 4x_forensic_coc (PostToolUse/SubagentStop hooks). Loaded only at hook trigger.
load_strategy_by_type.memory_skills: HONEY.md, NECTAR.md loaded per-session at /faerie startup (context budget <50 tokens; not per-skill).
load_strategy_by_type.no_preload_skills: Even frequently-used skills (/run, /spawn) are loaded on-demand from disk.

token_cost_per_skill.most_skills: 0 tokens at rest, 100–500 tokens on invocation (depends on SKILL.md size + execution)
token_cost_per_skill.heavy_skills: /data-ingest (SKILL.md ≈ 300 lines), /vision-ingest (≈ 400 lines), spawn (≈ 200 lines) = 1–3K tokens consumed during execution, not rest
token_cost_per_skill.memory_overhead: Global HONEY.md (~5K tokens) loaded once per session; project HONEY.md (~800 tokens) per-project. These are NOT per-skill costs.

section_1_token_cost_analysis.conclusion: Skills are a zero-cost-at-rest, pay-as-you-go model. The orchestration burden on main context is delegated to manifest-based coordination (forensics/), not skill registry caching.

onboarding_substrate_template.contents:
ONBOARDING SUBSTRATE FOR NEW MODELS — Template

## Model Card Integration

**Model Name:** [e.g., mistral-7b, llama2-70b, qwen-72b]
**Family:** [llama | mistral | qwen | dbrx | falcon]
**Context Window:** [4K | 8K | 16K | 32K+]
**Quantization:** [fp16 | int8 | int4]
**Deployment:** [Ollama | vLLM | TGI | Replicate]

## FAERIE CONTEXT INJECTION (Required)

### 1. Compass Navigation Protocol

Every agent spawned with this model receives:
- **Investigation Label:** investigation_label (string, clusters related work)
- **Compass Bearing Instructions:** "You are navigating via compass edges (N/S/E/W). After completing your primary task, write manifest with: compass_edge (bearing), next_task_queued (routing), discovered_work (if found during frontier scan)."
- **Manifest Schema:** (JSON; see example below)

### 2. Reputation Context

```json
{
  "composite_score": 0.72,
  "belief_index": 0.65,
  "interpretation": "Healthy (≥0.5). This model can be trusted with HIGH/CRITICAL phases. Honesty signal is medium; validate key claims."
}
```

Model must read composite_score and self-select work difficulty:
- Score ≥0.7: Can claim HIGH/CRITICAL phases
- Score 0.5–0.7: Claim MED phases, avoid CRITICAL
- Score <0.5: Recovery mode, narrow/modular work only

### 3. Manifest Writing Template

After task completion, model MUST emit JSON manifest:

```json
{
  "task_id": "<uuid or task name>",
  "dashboard_line": "<80-char summary of outcome>",
  "compass_edge": "S | N | E | W",
  "next_task_queued": "<task_id of next work, if any>",
  "discovered_work": {
    "found": true | false,
    "work_description": "<if found>",
    "matches_capability": true | false
  },
  "quality_score": 0.75,
  "belief_index": 0.68
}
```

Write to: `{repo}/forensics/manifests/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{TIMESTAMP}_manifest_task-{task_id}_{model_name}_{counter}.json`

### 4. Bundle Reading (Prompt Prefix)

Every spawn includes:

```
## CONTEXT BUNDLE — [investigation_label]

### HONEY (Crystallized Facts)
[Global + project HONEY.md injected here]

### NECTAR (Recent Findings)
[NECTAR.md tail-50 injected]

### POLLEN (Live Session Insights)
[MEM blocks from current session]

### INVESTIGATION CONTEXT
[Prior manifests in same investigation_label]

---

## YOUR TASK
[Task description + role-specific instructions]
```

Model must read and internalize all four layers before executing task.

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] Model reads bundle without errors
- [ ] Model writes valid JSON manifest (schema validation)
- [ ] Model identifies next_task_queued correctly (graph understanding)
- [ ] Model discovers related work (frontier scan, investigation_label matching)
- [ ] Model computes quality_score and belief_index (self-assessment)
- [ ] Model respects reputation gate (declines HIGH if score <0.5)
- [ ] Manifest readable by downstream agents (JSON format, <5KB)

## Deployment Checklist

- [ ] Register model in ~/.claude/agents/ (create .md agent card)
- [ ] Add to reputation framework (daily updates via 0x_reputation_summary.py)
- [ ] Test single spawn via /spawn skill
- [ ] Test team dispatch (4-agent team with new model)
- [ ] Measure FFMx (force per token, cost per outcome)
- [ ] Monitor manifest truthfulness (belief_index drift)

## CULTURAL COMPATIBILITY GAPS (See Section 4)

[Auto-filled by cultural audit]

section_4_cultural_compatibility_report.title: CULTURAL COMPATIBILITY REPORT: Claude CLI → Open Models
section_4_cultural_compatibility_report.scope: System optimization for Claude CLI + Claude models. What breaks with open models (Ollama llama2/mistral, vLLM, TGI)?

gap_1_agent_tool_replacement.what_breaks: Agent() is Claude CLI–specific tool. Open models have no native 'spawn subagent' mechanism.
gap_1_agent_tool_replacement.impact: Cannot spawn worker agents dynamically. W1 LIFTOFF (4–6 parallel agents) becomes W0 SINGLE (one model at a time).

implementation: Wrap Celery (task queue) in a Python library mimicking Agent() interface
Agent(subagent_type='llama2', prompt=..., model='llama2-70b') → queues job to Celery, polls until done
Register worker pool: Docker containers or K8s pods running vLLM/Ollama endpoints
Return result as manifest JSON (same schema as Claude agents)
recommended_fix.cost: 1–2 weeks to implement, 2–4 GB RAM overhead per worker

gap_2_reputation_framework.what_breaks: composite_score and belief_index are computed from Claude eval infrastructure (not available for open models).
gap_2_reputation_framework.impact: Cannot gate HIGH/CRITICAL work to healthy agents; no self-selection mechanism.

implementation: Track agent performance in Redis (task_id → outcome quality + manifest truthfulness)
Compute rolling average: quality_score (0.0–1.0) per agent per phase
belief_index = 4-signal: (1) manifest vs. actual outcome alignment, (2) error admission rate, (3) citation accuracy, (4) downstream task success
Serve scores via HTTP endpoint; agents fetch on startup
recommended_fix.cost: 1 week to implement; 500 MB Redis storage for 100+ agents

gap_3_free_model_integration.what_breaks: vision-ingest Step 4 (Vision API) and data-ingest agent spawning assume paid Claude API.
gap_3_free_model_integration.impact: Blocks vision-ingest pipeline unless Ollama+LLaVA configured; blocks data-ingest team dispatch.

recommended_fixes.solution: Ollama + LLaVA (or BLIP) adapter in vision-ingest Step 4
recommended_fixes.effort: 1 day (Python wrapper for Ollama HTTP endpoint)

recommended_fixes.solution: Use Celery task queue instead of Agent() tool
recommended_fixes.effort: 3–4 days (rewire data-ingest to emit task specs instead of Agent() calls)

gap_4_bundle_context_injection.recommendation: No change needed. Open models can read HONEY + NECTAR + pollen just like Claude models.

gap_5_manifest_schema.recommendation: Ensure model training includes manifest examples in prompt. Template provided in Section 3.

gap_6_token_cost_tracking.what_breaks: Claude Code CLI tracks tokens natively. Open models (Ollama, vLLM, TGI) have no standard accounting.
gap_6_token_cost_tracking.impact: Cannot measure FFMx (force per token, cost per outcome).

implementation: Wrap model calls in Python; log request tokens + response tokens to Prometheus
Export to /metrics dashboard (reuse existing /stat skill infrastructure)

compatibility_summary.difficulty_0_3: Architectural fit is good; 80% of system is model-agnostic
compatibility_summary.difficulty_to_adapt: Moderate. 2–3 weeks to build Celery bridge + reputation service + metrics hooks
recommended_rollout: Phase 1 (Week 1): Adapt audio-ingest + vision-ingest Steps 1–3 (no Agent() needed)
Phase 2 (Week 2): Build Celery bridge adapter + test with single llama2-70b worker
Phase 3 (Week 3): Build reputation scoring service; test team dispatch (4 agents)
Phase 4 (Week 4): Integrate metrics hooks; measure FFMx; stress-test multi-wave spawning

key_findings: 1. Skills cost ZERO tokens at rest (lazy load on invocation only)
2. Data skills use FREE local models (audio-ingest 100%, vision-ingest Steps 1–3, db-reconstruct conditional)
3. Vision-ingest Step 4 (extraction) requires paid API unless Ollama fallback enabled
4. Data-ingest orchestration is tightly coupled to Claude CLI Agent() tool (hard blocker for open models)
5. Reputation framework (composite_score, belief_index) is Claude eval–specific (needs adapter for open models)
6. Manifest schema + COC logging + forensic infrastructure is model-agnostic (no changes needed)
7. Open model support requires 2–3 weeks engineering + Celery bridge + reputation service (medium effort)
8. Faerie2 is architecturally sound for multi-model rosters; tight coupling is at orchestration layer, not data layer
